page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It has dedicated CPU allocation with hyperthreading enabled. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration included with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, both cached and uncached, fall within the average range. The instance demonstrates average performance across standard workloads such as Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and prompt processing for medium-sized large language models represent performance bottlenecks, scoring in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the n2d-highmem-8 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, medium-scale web serving, and memory-intensive data processing tasks. The lack of local storage means persistent storage must be attached network-wise, which should be factored into architectural planning.
